header: House prep recipes for the modern bar core (after 20261018010000). Stage
* 38 shared catalog preps that had no recipe get one, each from the pages
it cites (one item_sources row per recipe, yield and keep fact; two
sites for the staples): cordials, orgeats, acid solutions, a house
falernum (now a kind of Falernum), house grenadine (now a kind of
Grenadine), oleos, honey syrups, sherbets, fruit syrups and shrubs.
One new row: Malic acid solution (10%). One new plain ingredient:
* Seven bar blends (Vermouth blend, Sherry blend and the like) get the
Mix tag only: their amounts are each bar's own.
* A keep is the shortest any cited page gives for that recipe or a less
preserved one; with nothing to cite there's no keep.
* An independent second check of 100 random facts against the cited
pages found 1 wrong (1%): a keep longer than the page's shortest. It is

ingredients.name: Wild blueberry
ingredients.description: Small lowbush blueberries, sold fresh or frozen, with a deeper colour and sharper flavour than cultivated blueberries.

preps.name: Apple cordial
preps.description: A sharp green apple cordial: filtered Granny Smith juice with sugar at 40% of its weight and a blend of malic, citric and ascorbic acid. Built for a crisp, clear Apple Martini.

recipe.note: freshly juiced and filtered clear, or clear 100% apple juice

steps.body: Juice the apples and pass the juice through a fine sieve, then a coffee filter, until it runs clear. Weigh it.
Stir the sugar with half the juice over low heat just until it dissolves, then take it off the heat and add the rest of the juice.
Weigh the mix and stir in the malic, citric and ascorbic acid until dissolved. Bottle and chill.

sources.note: Punch (Ramsey Musk's clarified sour apple cordial): sugar at 40% of the juice weight, then 3% malic, 0.5% ascorbic and 1.5% citric acid by weight of the juice and sugar mix. Scaled to 500 g juice (700 g mix).

preps.name: Apple shrub
preps.description: Shredded whole apples steeped two days with cider vinegar, raw sugar and cinnamon, then pressed and strained. A spiced, tart base for highballs and whisky drinks.

recipe.note: medium, quartered, core and seeds left in

steps.body: Shred the quartered apples on a box grater or in a food processor.
Mix the apple, vinegar, sugar and cinnamon sticks in a non-reactive tub, cover and leave somewhere cool for up to 2 days.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the apple to get all the liquid out. Discard the solids.
Bottle, shake to mix and keep in the fridge. Bin it if it turns bubbly, cloudy or slimy, or shows mould.

sources.note: UC ANR Master Food Preservers (El Dorado), Cinnamon-Apple Shrub after Michael Dietsch: 3 medium apples, 1 cup cider vinegar, 1/2 cup turbinado, 2 cinnamon sticks. Cups at 240 ml, sugar at 200 g a cup.
This Cinnamon-Apple Shrub recipe, refrigerated: up to one year (52 weeks).

preps.name: Apricot syrup
preps.description: Diced fresh apricots simmered in 1:1 syrup and strained. For sours, spritzes and tonic highballs.

steps.body: Bring apricots, sugar and water to the boil, stirring just until the sugar dissolves.
Turn down and simmer.
Take off the heat and cool.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit. Close the jar once cool and keep cold.

sources.note: 1 cup diced apricots (4 to 5 fruit), 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, simmered 10 minutes, cooled 10, strained. Doubled; 1 cup sugar taken as 200 g, 1 cup as 240 ml.
1 2/3 cups per batch; doubled is about 800 ml.
Two weeks in the fridge, given for this same recipe.

preps.name: Banana oleo saccharum
preps.description: Ripe banana peels cured in an equal weight of sugar until they give up a soft, tropical syrup. Use it in place of some of the simple syrup in a Daiquiri or Old Fashioned, and it puts peels from banana prep to work.

steps.body: Chop the ripe banana peels into 1 cm pieces and weigh them.
Seal the peels with an equal weight of sugar in a jar or bag and shake to coat.
Leave at room temperature for 24 to 48 hours, until the sugar has turned to syrup.
Strain out all the solids and bottle the syrup. Keep it cold.

sources.note: 250 g chopped ripe banana peel to 250 g white sugar (1 : 1 by weight), sealed 24 to 48 hours, then strained. Agrees exactly with Punch; we use this one.
Project Halcyon (Manchester): 250 g banana peels to 250 g sugar, sealed in a bag for 48 hours, strained and refrigerated. Same 1 : 1 ratio as Campari Academy.
Keep for this same 1 : 1 banana peel recipe: fridge, 1 to 2 weeks. We use the shorter end, 1 week.

preps.name: Blackberry shrub
preps.description: Equal parts blackberries, sugar and cider vinegar: berries macerated with sugar, then rested with vinegar and strained. A deep purple, jammy-tart syrup for sodas and bramble-style drinks.

steps.body: Mash the blackberries with the sugar and leave in the fridge for a few hours or overnight.
Stir in the vinegar and return to the fridge for a few hours up to a few days, depending on how sharp you want it.
Strain out the solids and bottle in glass. Keep cold.

sources.note: CUESA (Foodwise): 1 cup each of blackberries, sugar and cider vinegar (1 : 1 : 1 by volume), the common ratio UC ANR also names. Doubled; cups at 240 ml, sugar at 200 g a cup.
About 3 cups per cup of each; doubled to about 1.44 litres.
This blackberry shrub recipe: about a month in the fridge.
UC ANR Master Food Preservers general shrub storage, for cold-process shrubs at 1:1:1 fruit, sugar, vinegar.

preps.name: Blueberry syrup
preps.description: Wild blueberries simmered in 1:1 syrup and pressed through a sieve, deep purple and jammy. For sours, lemonades and sodas.

recipe.note: fresh or frozen (2 cups); the source allows twice the volume of regular blueberries

steps.body: Bring blueberries, sugar and water to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Turn down and simmer.
Take off the heat and cool 10 to 15 minutes.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the berries. Close the jar once fully cool and keep cold.

sources.note: 1 cup wild blueberries (or 2 cups regular), 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, simmered 15 minutes and strained. Doubled with wild berries; 1 cup sugar taken as 200 g, 1 cup as 240 ml.
1 2/3 cups per batch; doubled is about 800 ml.
Two weeks in the fridge, given for this same recipe.

preps.name: Cherry syrup
preps.description: Halved pitted cherries simmered in 1:1 syrup, mashed and strained. For cherry sours, old fashioneds, Shirley Temples and sodas.

recipe.note: pitted and halved, fresh or frozen (2 cups)

steps.body: Bring sugar, water and cherries to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Simmer gently; don't let it boil hard.
Off the heat, mash the cherries and let it stand.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the fruit. Close the jar once cool and keep cold.

sources.note: 1 cup sugar, 1 cup halved pitted cherries, 1 cup water, simmered 10 minutes, cooled 10, strained. Doubled; 1 cup sugar taken as 200 g, 1 cup as 240 ml.
Same 1 : 1 : 1 by volume (cherries, water, sugar), simmered 10 minutes, mashed and rested 15 minutes before straining.
1 1/3 cups per batch; doubled is about 640 ml.
Two weeks in the fridge, given for this same recipe.

preps.name: Citrus cordial
preps.description: A lemon and lime cordial: zest simmered in a sugar syrup, sharpened with citric and tartaric acid, then finished with the fresh juice. For highballs, gimlet riffs and long no-alcohol drinks.

steps.body: Put the lime and lemon zest, sugar and water in a pan and bring to the boil.
Turn the heat down and simmer gently.
Stir in the citric and tartaric acid and take the pan off the heat.
Add the lime and lemon juice, strain out the zest and bottle in sterilised bottles.

sources.note: Miele recipe: zest and juice of 5 limes and 3 lemons, 660 g sugar, 625 ml water, 1 tsp citric acid, 2 tsp tartaric acid; zest simmered 5 minutes in the syrup, acids then juice added, strained. Used as given.
The page gives the recipe size as 1 litre.

preps.name: Ginger honey
preps.description: Honey syrup simmered with fresh ginger, then strained: sweet, warm and peppery. The one bottle a Penicillin or a hot toddy needs.

steps.body: Peel the ginger and cut it into 1 cm chunks.
Bring the ginger, honey and water to a low boil, then turn down and simmer gently, stirring now and then.
Take it off the heat and let it stand before straining.
Strain out the ginger, cool and bottle. Shake before use, as it settles.

sources.note: 120 g honey, 50 g fresh ginger, 120 g water (1 : 0.42 : 1 by weight), simmered 10 minutes, rested 10, strained; scaled to 600 g honey. Feast and West runs wetter (1 cup honey to 1.5 cups water); we use Modernist Pantry's weighed ratio.
1 cup honey, 1.5 cups water, a 4 inch piece of ginger simmered 10 to 15 minutes. Its honey to water runs about 1 : 1.5 by volume against Modernist Pantry's 1 : 1; we use Modernist Pantry's.
Keep for Feast and West's honey ginger syrup, which has more water (less sugar) than ours, so it carries over: fridge, up to 2 weeks.

preps.name: Grapefruit cordial
preps.description: Grapefruit juice warmed with sugar and peel, then sharpened with citric acid. A bright, bitter-edged cordial for Palomas, spritzes and Americano riffs.

recipe.note: clarified in the source; at least fine strained

steps.body: Put the grapefruit juice, sugar and peel in a pot and bring just to a simmer.
Take it off the heat and stir until all the sugar has dissolved.
Strain out the peel.
Stir in the citric acid, let it cool, then bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Mike Capoferri (Thunderbolt, Los Angeles): 500 g clarified grapefruit juice, 450 g sugar, 25 g peel, 10 g citric acid. Used as written.
Second source runs about 40 oz juice to 30 oz sugar and 1 oz citric acid, then reduces it by half; we use Thunderbolt's unreduced 0.9 : 1 sugar to juice.

preps.name: Grapefruit shrub
preps.description: Grapefruit peel muddled into sugar for its oil, then segments and cider vinegar steeped two to four days in the fridge. Bitter-bright, for Palomas, sodas and spritzes.

recipe.note: whole peel of 1 medium grapefruit, little pith

steps.body: Muddle the sugar with the grapefruit peel to work the oils out.
Add the segments, muddle again and leave for 10 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar, cover and steep in the fridge for 2 to 4 days: shorter for a sharper shrub.
Strain out the solids, bottle and keep cold.

sources.note: The Little Epicurean: 1 cup sugar, peel of 1 medium grapefruit, 1 cup segments, 1 cup cider vinegar, steeped 2 to 4 days cold. Cups at 240 ml, sugar at 200 g a cup; segments kept as a volume.
UC ANR Master Food Preservers general shrub storage, for cold-process shrubs at about 1:1:1 fruit, sugar, vinegar, which this recipe is.

preps.name: House falernum
preps.description: A house falernum: overproof rum steeped with lime zest, ginger, clove and nutmeg, then married with rich syrup. The spiced lime sweetener for Corn 'n' Oil, Zombies and other tiki drinks.

steps.body: Combine the rum, cloves, lime zest, ginger and nutmeg in a sealed container and leave for 24 hours. Overproof rum: keep it well away from flames and hot burners.
Strain the infusion through a fine sieve.
Make a rich syrup: stir the sugar into the hot water until fully dissolved, then cool.
Blend the strained infusion with the cooled syrup and let it rest for several hours before using. Keep chilled.

sources.note: Adam Bernbach (2 Birds 1 Stone) via Punch: 8 oz overproof rum, 40 cloves, zest of 10 limes, 3 oz ginger, 1/4 nutmeg, steeped 24 h, then rich syrup of 20 oz sugar to 10 oz water. Ounces read as 240 ml rum, 85 g ginger, 567 g sugar, 284 g water.
The Punch recipe yields about 3 cups (720 ml).
Keep given for this exact Punch recipe (the one we use): up to one month refrigerated, airtight.

preps.name: House-made grenadine
preps.description: Real grenadine from pomegranate juice and sugar, deepened with pomegranate molasses and a little orange flower water. Made cold, so it keeps the fresh fruit flavour for Jack Roses, Tequila Sunrises and Ward Eights.

steps.body: Combine the pomegranate juice and sugar in a bottle or jar and shake until the sugar dissolves.
Add the pomegranate molasses and shake well; it dissolves faster if the juice is at room temperature.
Add orange flower water to taste, then refrigerate. Extra can be frozen.

sources.note: Imbibe: 8 oz pomegranate juice, 1 cup superfine sugar, 2 oz pomegranate molasses, 1 to 3 tsp orange flower water (optional). Converted to 240 ml, 200 g, 60 ml, 5 ml and doubled. Optional vodka left out.
Keep given for this Imbibe recipe (the one we use, made without the optional vodka): use within 2 weeks refrigerated.

preps.name: Jasmine cordial
preps.description: A floral cordial of jasmine flowers and jasmine green tea, steeped gently sous vide in a light citric syrup. For highballs with tequila, gin or soda.

steps.body: Put everything in a vacuum bag and seal.
Cook sous vide at 50°C.
Strain out the flowers and tea, bottle and chill.

sources.note: Koppert Cress (Andrea Arcaini, Rita Cocktails Milano): 140 g caster sugar, 280 ml water, 3 g jasmine flowers, 9 g jasmine green tea, 5 g citric acid, sealed and cooked sous vide 1 h at 50°C. Doubled.

preps.name: Lemon cordial
preps.description: A sweet-sharp lemon concentrate made Morgenthaler's way: sugar, hot water, juice, zest and citric acid blended and strained. Keeps far longer than juice and goes into gimlet-style drinks and highballs.

steps.body: Put the sugar, hot water, lemon juice, grated zest and citric acid in a blender.
Blend on medium for 30 seconds, until the sugar and acid have dissolved.
Pass through a fine strainer to take out the zest.
Bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Morgenthaler's lime cordial: 250 g sugar, 240 ml hot water, 45 ml juice, 8 g grated peel, 25 g citric acid; he confirms lemon swapped in like for like works. Doubled. Second source (Bonnie's, StarChefs) is juice heavy with no acid; we use this one.
Channing Centeno (Bonnie's, New York): 1.5 kg sugar steeped overnight with the peel of 12 lemons, then 2 quarts lemon juice, no acid. Far more juice than Morgenthaler's; we use Morgenthaler's ratio.
About 12 fl oz (360 ml) per batch; doubled to 720 ml.
The author's answers in the page's comments run from a week or more to two weeks; we take the shorter, a week.

preps.name: Lemon oleo
preps.description: Lemon rinds cured in white and demerara sugar for a day, then loosened with boiling water into a pourable lemon oil syrup. A punch base that gets more out of the lemons you squeeze.

steps.body: Put the lemon rinds in a jar with both sugars and leave for 24 hours.
Pour boiling water over the sugar and rinds and stir until the sugar has dissolved.
Strain out the rinds and bottle the syrup. Keep it cold.

sources.note: Half a cup (125 ml) lemon rinds, 2/3 cup fine white sugar, 1/6 cup demerara, 1 cup (250 ml) boiling water after a 24 hour cure. Sugar converted at 1 cup about 200 g (133 g and 33 g).
The recipe states it makes 1 cup (250 ml).
Keep for this same LCBO lemon oleo recipe: up to 2 weeks in the fridge.

preps.name: Lime sherbet
preps.description: Lime peel cured in sugar overnight, then dissolved in an equal weight of fresh lime juice: a sweet and sour lime syrup with the oil of the peel in it. Lime peel runs bitter, so taste before you commit it to a drink. Starting point: test a batch first.

recipe.note: peels of the limes you juice, thin, as little pith as possible

steps.body: Peel the limes thinly, leaving the white pith behind (it makes lime sherbet bitter), then juice and strain them.
Muddle the peels into the sugar, cover and leave at room temperature, stirring now and then, until the oil has turned the sugar to syrup.
Lift out the peels and stir in the juice until the sugar dissolves. Warm it gently if needed, but never boil.
Bottle and keep cold.

sources.note: Citrus sherbet: peels in sugar at least 24 hours, then juice equal to the sugar; peel as much fruit as you juice. Names lime and warns its peel is more bitter. Scaled to 500 g sugar and 500 ml lime juice.
Lemon sherbet: 120 g caster sugar, peel of 2 lemons, 120 ml lemon juice (1 : 1 sugar to juice), dissolved without boiling. Same ratio we apply to lime.
Keep for Cocktails and Bars' lemon sherbet at the same 1 : 1 sugar to juice; lemon is no more acidic than lime, so it carries over: about 2 weeks in the fridge.

preps.name: Lychee syrup
preps.description: A floral syrup of lychees simmered in a little under 1:1 sugar syrup, then chilled and strained. For lychee martinis, highballs and spritzes.

recipe.note: peeled and pitted, fresh or canned

steps.body: Bring the water and sugar to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the lychees, pressing them lightly, and simmer until the syrup lightly coats a spoon, like thin maple syrup.
Pour syrup and fruit into a jar and let cool.
Chill with the fruit in so the flavour carries through.
Strain into a clean bottle, pressing the lychees lightly. Keep cold.

sources.note: 125 ml water, 100 g sugar and 12 lychees, simmered until it coats a spoon, chilled 1 hour, strained. Scaled four times.
A lychee and ginger syrup: 1.5 cups each of sugar and water (about 300 g to 360 ml, 0.83 : 1) with 3 cups lychee. Its sugar to water ratio agrees with the 0.8 : 1 we use from Sift and Simmer.
One week in the fridge, given for this same recipe.

preps.name: Makrut lime leaf cordial
preps.description: A lemon cordial steeped overnight with makrut lime leaves and ginger and sharpened with tartaric acid. The leaves give the lime perfume; lemon and acid carry the sourness.

recipe.note: scrubbed, zested and juiced; squeezed halves steeped then lifted out

steps.body: Put the lemon zest, juice and squeezed halves, lime leaves, ginger and sugar in a heatproof bowl.
Pour over the boiling water and stir until the sugar dissolves. Cool a little, cover and steep in the fridge overnight.
Lift out the lemon halves, leaves and ginger.
Stir in the tartaric acid, bottle and keep cold. Shake before pouring.

sources.note: SBS Food (Feast magazine, Feb 2014): 4 lemons, 4 makrut lime leaves, 3 cm ginger, 700 g caster sugar, 1 L boiling water, 50 g tartaric acid; steeped overnight in the fridge. Used as given.
Makes 1.2 L of cordial.

preps.name: Malic acid solution (10%)
preps.description: Malic acid dissolved in water at the bar strength of 1 part acid to 10 parts water by weight, which bars call a 10% solution. It adds a green apple style sourness a dash at a time, or acid to batched drinks without citrus.

steps.body: Weigh the malic acid and pour over the hot water.
Whisk until fully dissolved, then cool.
Bottle in glass rather than plastic or metal, and label with the strength.

sources.note: Team Lyan's 10% malic solution: 10 g malic acid to 100 g water, whisked and bottled. Scaled x5 to 50 g acid in 500 g water. Keep solutions in glass.
Same strength: 10 g malic acid to 100 ml boiling water, stirred to dissolve, stored airtight at room temperature, called non perishable (no time given).

preps.name: Mandarin cordial
preps.description: Fresh mandarin juice boiled with an oleo saccharum made from the peels, plus citric acid. Carries the peel's perfume as well as the juice, for spritzes and gin drinks.

steps.body: Muddle the mandarin peels with the sugar in a sealed container to release their oils, then leave 24 hours.
Lift out the peels and add the oily sugar to the strained mandarin juice.
Add the citric acid and bring to the boil, stirring until the sugar and acid have dissolved.
Let it cool and pour into a clean bottle.

sources.note: THE DUKE gin: 250 ml mandarin juice, an oleo of 6 to 7 peels with 125 g sugar (24 h), 5 g citric acid. Doubled to 500 ml juice, 12 peels.

preps.name: Mandarin shrub
preps.description: Mandarin juice and peel blitzed with raw sugar and steeped overnight with champagne vinegar. Bright and usable at once, rounder after a few weeks in the bottle.

steps.body: Blitz the sugar and mandarin peel for about 10 seconds to a coarse, wet pulp.
Tip into a bowl and stir in the lemon zest, mandarin juice and vinegar until the sugar dissolves.
Cover with a clean cloth and leave at room temperature overnight.
Strain through a fine sieve into a sterilised bottle, seal and refrigerate. Use now or rest 3 to 4 weeks to mellow.

sources.note: Pip Magazine, after Holly Davis's Ferment: 660 g raw sugar, peel of 6 mandarins, zest of 1 lemon, 750 ml mandarin juice, 500 ml champagne or white wine vinegar. Used as given.
About 1 litre per batch.
This mandarin shrub recipe: up to 12 months refrigerated (12 x 4 weeks).
UC ANR Master Food Preservers general shrub storage, for shrubs of fruit, sugar and vinegar kept in the fridge.

preps.name: Mango syrup
preps.description: Diced ripe mango simmered in 1:1 syrup and pressed through a sieve. For mango daiquiris, margaritas, mojitos and sodas.

recipe.note: diced, ripe, fresh or frozen (2 cups)

steps.body: Bring sugar, water and mango to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Turn down and simmer.
Take off the heat and cool.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the mango hard. Close the jar once cool and keep cold.

sources.note: 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 1 cup diced mango, simmered 15 minutes and strained. Doubled; 1 cup sugar taken as 200 g, 1 cup as 240 ml.
Second source is a blended, unstrained mango nectar: 3/4 cup of 1:1 syrup to 1 cup mango, so about half the sugar per cup of fruit. We use the strained syrup ratio from The Healthful Ideas.
1.5 cups per batch; doubled is 3 cups, about 720 ml.
Two weeks in the fridge, given for this same recipe.
One week in the fridge, given for the blended mango nectar (less sugar, uncooked). We keep the shorter figure.

preps.name: Orange cordial
preps.description: Fresh orange juice, water and sugar with citric and malic acid added, since orange alone lacks the sourness of lemon or lime. Built for long drinks and highballs.

steps.body: Put the orange juice, water, sugar, citric acid and malic acid in a pot.
Warm, stirring, until the sugar has dissolved.
Take it off the heat, let it cool and bottle.

sources.note: Tristan K Joseph (Civil Liberties, Toronto): 600 g orange juice, 600 ml water, 600 g sugar, 30 g citric acid, 15 g malic acid. Used as written.
Second source is a home cordial for diluting with water: 300 ml juice, 2.5 cups sugar, 2 cups water, 2 tsp tartaric acid, so much less juice; we use Civil Liberties' bar ratio.

preps.name: Orange syrup
preps.description: A 1:1 syrup simmered with orange zest and rested before the zest comes out. Adds orange oil and sweetness to sours, spritzes and coffee drinks.

recipe.note: zest of 2 oranges, cut with a peeler, white pith removed

steps.body: Cut the zest with a peeler and trim off the white pith, which is bitter.
Bring sugar, water and zest to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Simmer gently.
Off the heat, rest 10 to 15 minutes, then lift out the zest. Close the jar once cool and keep cold.

sources.note: 1 cup sugar, 1 cup water and the zest of 1 orange, simmered 15 minutes and rested before removing the zest. Doubled; 1 cup sugar taken as 200 g, 1 cup as 240 ml.
1 1/3 cups per batch; doubled is about 640 ml.
Two weeks in the fridge, given for this same recipe.

preps.name: Pear shrub
preps.description: A cold-process drinking vinegar of ripe pear, sugar and cider vinegar, left a week in the fridge so the fruit softens the vinegar. For highballs, sodas and autumn sours.

recipe.note: very ripe Bartlett, peeled, 1 cm dice (2 cups by volume)

steps.body: Put the diced pear, sugar and vinegar in a clean jar and seal it.
Leave in the fridge for 5 to 7 days, giving it a gentle stir once a day so the sugar dissolves.
Strain out the fruit through a fine sieve, bottle and keep cold. Bin it if it fizzes hard or smells off.

sources.note: 2 cups diced ripe pear, 1 cup sugar, 1 cup cider vinegar (2 : 1 : 1 by volume), a week in the fridge. Cups converted at 240 ml, sugar at 200 g a cup; pear kept as a volume.
This pear shrub recipe: the method says 3 months, the recipe notes say 1 month; we take the shorter.
UC ANR Master Food Preservers general shrub storage, for cold-process shrubs at 1:1:1 or 2:1:1 fruit, sugar, vinegar.

preps.name: Pepita orgeat
preps.description: A nut-free orgeat made from hulled pumpkin seeds blended with water and sugar, giving a green-tinged, savoury nutty syrup. Use it where you would use almond orgeat, or for guests with tree nut allergies.

steps.body: Blend the pepitas to a fine powder.
With the blender on low, add the water slowly until fully combined.
Still on low, add the sugar slowly until dissolved.
Strain through a coffee filter, bottle and chill.

sources.note: Punch (Kevin Diedrich, Pacific Cocktail Haven): 4 oz pepitas, 8 oz water, 8 oz sugar, read as weight: 113 g, 227 g, 227 g (1 : 2 : 2).
The Punch recipe yields 12 oz (about 360 ml).

preps.name: Pistachio orgeat
preps.description: An orgeat made with pistachios in place of almonds: a blended nut milk sweetened into a creamy syrup. Swap it in for almond orgeat in Mai Tais, Saturn riffs and sours.

steps.body: Blend the pistachios with the near-boiling water on high for 2 full minutes; the longer the blend, the smoother the syrup.
Strain through a nut-milk bag, or a fine sieve lined with several layers of cheesecloth, and discard the solids.
Return the nut milk to the blender, add the sugar and blend for another minute until dissolved.
Bottle in glass, chill, and shake before each use as it can separate.

sources.note: The Merchant (Madison) via Imbibe: 3 cups near-boiling water, 7 oz pistachios, 2 1/4 cups sugar; converted to 720 ml, 198 g (weight ounces) and 450 g. Optional gum stabilisers left out.
American Pistachios runs 200 g pistachios, 660 g very hot water, 500 g demerara, the same blend-strain-blend method and within about 10% of the Imbibe ratio we use.
The Imbibe recipe makes 1 quart (about 945 ml).
Keep given for this exact Imbibe recipe (the one we use): up to 1 month refrigerated.

preps.name: Pomegranate syrup
preps.description: A plain, rich pomegranate syrup: fresh juice with twice its volume of sugar, warmed only until dissolved. A simple grenadine for any drink that wants clean pomegranate sweetness.

steps.body: Pour the pomegranate juice into a saucepan and gradually stir in the sugar.
Warm gently until the sugar dissolves; do not let it simmer.
Cool, fine strain into a clean bottle and refrigerate. Mind the use-by date of the juice.

sources.note: Difford's: 2 cups sugar to 1 cup pomegranate juice, warmed until dissolved without simmering. Converted (1 cup 240 ml, 1 cup sugar 200 g) and doubled to 480 ml juice, 800 g sugar.
Keep given for this exact Difford's recipe (the one we use): about a week refrigerated.

preps.name: Recomposed lime
preps.description: A clear lime juice stand-in built from citric and malic acid in water, matching the acid make-up of fresh lime. It has the sourness but none of lime's sugar or peel aroma, so it bolsters juice or replaces it in clear and batched drinks.

steps.body: Weigh the citric and malic acid into the filtered water.
Stir until both acids have fully dissolved, then bottle and label.
Use it like lime juice, but taste the drink: it is sour without lime's sweetness, so you may want a touch more syrup.

sources.note: Dave Arnold's lime acid (Liquid Intelligence) as quoted: 94 g water, 4 g citric, 2 g malic, 0.04 g succinic (optional, left out here). Scaled x10 to 940 g water, 40 g citric, 20 g malic.
Confirms the target: lime juice is about 4% citric and 2% malic acid, the same 2:1 split used here.

preps.name: Rhubarb cordial
preps.description: Rhubarb simmered with sugar, lemon and a little ginger, then strained to a pink, tart cordial. Lengthen with soda or use in spritzes and sours.

recipe.note: optional, thumb-sized piece, peeled and finely grated

steps.body: Put the rhubarb, sugar, ginger, lemon zest and juice and water in a pan and bring to the boil.
Simmer until the rhubarb is soft and the sugar has dissolved.
Strain through a sieve without pressing; let it drip for a clearer cordial.
Stir in the citric acid, bottle in sterilised bottles and chill.

sources.note: Jo's Kitchen Larder: 500 g rhubarb, 250 g sugar, 400 ml water, 1 lemon, optional ginger, simmered 10 to 15 minutes and strained; the author adds 1 tsp citric acid for this batch to keep it longer. Used as given.
The author says the recipe makes roughly a 700 ml bottle.
Two weeks in the fridge for this same recipe without citric acid (less preserved than ours). The longer keep the author gives with acid is vague, so not used.

preps.name: Rhubarb shrub
preps.description: Chopped rhubarb steeped five days in white wine vinegar, strained and warmed with sugar. Pink, sharp and vegetal, for spritzes, sodas and gin drinks.

recipe.note: stalks only, chopped (1.5 cups by volume)

steps.body: Use the stalks only: rhubarb leaves are not edible. Put the chopped rhubarb in a jar, cover with the vinegar and seal.
Keep somewhere dark and cool for 5 days, shaking once a day.
Strain the vinegar into a pan, add the sugar and warm, stirring, until it has fully dissolved.
Cool, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: 1.5 cups chopped rhubarb steeped 5 days in 1 cup white wine vinegar, then warmed with 1 cup sugar. Cups at 240 ml, sugar at 200 g a cup; rhubarb kept as a volume.
UC ANR Master Food Preservers general shrub storage. Applied because this recipe carries more sugar and vinegar per unit of fruit than the 1:1:1 shrub UC ANR describes.

preps.name: Spiced honey
preps.description: Honey and sugar syrup simmered briefly with clove, star anise, cinnamon and allspice. A small measure warms up whisky drinks and autumn sours.

steps.body: Warm the water, honey and sugar over low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cloves, star anise, cinnamon and allspice.
Bring to the boil, then turn down and simmer.
Strain out the spices, cool to room temperature and bottle. Keep it cold.

sources.note: 1 cup (250 ml) water, 1 cup honey, 1 cup (250 g) sugar, 5 cloves, 5 star anise, 1 cinnamon stick, 5 allspice, simmered 3 minutes. The page prints honey as 375 ml, which clashes with its 1 cup; we use its 250 ml cup.

preps.name: Strawberry cordial
preps.description: Strawberries simmered in water and strained clear, then sweetened and sharpened with lemon and citric acid. A pink, fresh-tasting cordial for sodas, spritzes and long drinks.

recipe.note: washed, hulled, halved if large; pulp strained out

steps.body: Warm the strawberries in the water over a medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, pressing them gently as they soften.
Pour through a fine sieve or cloth and let it drip for about 30 minutes; don't squeeze, or it goes cloudy.
Return the strawberry water to the pan with the sugar, lemon juice and citric acid and stir over the heat until the sugar dissolves.
Pour hot into sterilised bottles, seal, cool, and keep in the fridge once opened.

sources.note: 1 kg strawberries simmered in 600 ml water and strained, then 500 g sugar, 2 tbsp (30 ml) lemon juice and 1 tsp citric acid. Used as written. Second source runs far sweeter; we use this one.
Second source macerates 500 g strawberries in 600 g sugar overnight, then simmers with 400 ml water, half a lemon and thyme: more than twice the sugar per berry. We use the 1 kg : 500 g recipe above.

preps.name: Verdita
preps.description: Pineapple juice blended with mint, coriander, lime and green chilli, then fine strained: the green Mexican chaser for a neat tequila or mezcal, and a bright mixer in a Margarita.

recipe.note: half to one, seeds out, diced, added to taste

steps.body: Blend the pineapple juice, the juice of one lime, the coriander and the mint until smooth.
Add a little jalapeño and blend again. Taste, then add more chilli or lime to balance heat and sharpness.
Fine strain into a clean glass bottle and keep cold. Shake gently before use.

sources.note: Tequila Tromba's verdita: 3 cups (750 ml) pineapple juice, juice of 1 or more limes, a large handful each of coriander and mint, half to 1 seeded jalapeño to taste. Amounts as given.
The recipe states it makes just over 3 cups (750 ml).
Keep for this same Tromba verdita recipe: refrigerate up to 3 days. Campari Academy's verdita (with cucumber and water) says serve within 24 hours.

preps.name: Watermelon cordial
preps.description: Watermelon blended with water and strained, then heated with sugar, citric acid and a little salt to lift the fruit. For watermelon sodas, Margaritas and highballs.

recipe.note: half a teaspoon per 200 g strained juice
a third of the strained juice weight

steps.body: Blend the watermelon flesh with half its weight in water until smooth, then strain out the pulp.
Weigh the juice: add 1% of that weight in salt, half a teaspoon of citric acid per 200 g and a third of the weight in sugar. The amounts listed assume about 1,200 g of juice.
Heat to just below a boil and hold 10 minutes, stirring until everything dissolves.
Cool, strain through muslin if you have it, bottle and keep in the fridge.

sources.note: Cameron Fielding: 400 g watermelon blended with 200 g water (gave 600 g juice), 1% salt, half a tsp citric acid per 200 g juice, a third the juice weight in sugar. Doubled. Second source differs; we use this one.
Second source simmers 800 g watermelon with 300 g sugar and 200 ml water, then adds 80 ml lemon juice: less sugar and water, lemon for acid. We use Smartblend's ratio.
With citric acid, 4+ weeks; with lime juice instead, 2 to 3 days.
Up to a week in the fridge in a glass bottle.

preps.name: Yuzu cordial
preps.description: Sliced whole yuzu macerated cold in sugar with a little salt and citric acid, then rinsed with hot water to pull out the last of the syrup. For chuhai, highballs and sours.

steps.body: Put the sliced yuzu, sugar, salt and citric acid in a non-reactive container, seal and shake until the fruit is coated.
Refrigerate for 3 days.
Strain, keeping the syrup and the solids apart.
Stir the solids with the hot water, strain again, then combine both liquids and bottle.

sources.note: StarChefs (Justin Kato, RYLA): 10 sliced yuzu, 500 g sugar, 5 g kosher salt, 5 g citric acid, 3 days in the fridge, solids rinsed with 250 g hot water. Source calls it yuzu syrup and gives a 32 oz (about 960 ml) yield. Used as given.

preps.name: Yuzu sherbet
preps.description: Yuzu peel cured in sugar overnight, then dissolved in an equal weight of yuzu juice for a fragrant, sharp citrus syrup. Built on the general citrus sherbet ratio, not a yuzu recipe. Starting point: test a batch first.

recipe.note: peels of the yuzu you juice, thin, as little pith as possible

steps.body: Peel the yuzu thinly, leaving the white pith behind, then juice and strain the fruit.
Muddle the peels into the sugar, cover and leave at room temperature, stirring now and then, until the oil has turned the sugar to syrup.
Lift out the peels and stir in the juice until the sugar dissolves. Warm it gently if needed, but never boil.
Bottle and keep cold.

sources.note: General citrus sherbet: peels in sugar at least 24 hours, then juice equal in amount to the sugar; peel as much fruit as you juice. Applied to yuzu at 250 g sugar to 250 ml juice; no source gives a yuzu version.
Lemon sherbet: 120 g caster sugar, peel of 2 lemons, 120 ml lemon juice (1 : 1 sugar to juice), dissolved without boiling. Same ratio we apply to yuzu.
Keep for Cocktails and Bars' lemon sherbet at the same 1 : 1 sugar to juice; lemon juice is no more acidic than yuzu, so it carries over: about 2 weeks in the fridge.
